speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Health what are the strategies to engage social media platforms and advertising on social media to raise awareness about the harms of vaping and to discourage the use of vapes and habit of vaping among youths in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: There is a global rise in the use of e-vaporisers among youths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Marketing, including through social media and influencers, is largely targeted at youths, which contributed to its widespread usage amongst this age group.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Many youths picked up the vaping habit, thinking it is harmless because it smells like fruits, and they make it a lifestyle habit among their friends.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: However, we all know that vaping is harmful.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The fact that it is taking root among youths makes it even more harmful.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Many countries allowed vaping, only to try to restrict its consumption now.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Fortunately, Singapore saw its potential harm and banned it from the start.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: As we all know, like all domestic laws, the Tobacco Act applies to vaping-related content published in Singapore and by Singapore-connected persons or entities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: However, the Internet and social media is a global ecosystem and having domestic laws that ban harmful content or advertisements does not mean that these materials would not come in from a foreign source or a foreign influencer.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: That is the nature of online enforcement today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: But we are not without agency and we have put in place several measures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Enforcement actions may be taken against platforms that are found with inadequate processes to detect and remove vaping-related contents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) and Health Sciences Authority (HSA) will continue to work closely with the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) and the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) to engage these platforms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The designated social media services are Facebook, HardwareZone, Instagram, TikTok, X and YouTube.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Thirdly, HSA has been monitoring illicit sales of e-vaporisers via social media, e-commerce and messaging platforms, and carrying out operations to remove e-vaporiser content.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Fourthly, even as we remove e-vaporisers content, we also try to increase pro-health content.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And I thank the Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the answer.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I think most of my supplementary questions have been answered, but just one more.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I spoke about this in Parliament in one of my speeches in the Committee of Supply.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There is a strong link between vaping and cannabis abuse.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In Canada, 29% of cannabis-using individuals aged 15 years or older indicated that vaping is their preferred method for cannabis use.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Will MOH conduct a study on this link and risks in terms of the usage of vaping and drug abuse?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Yes, there is a lot of research and data surrounding this information, and we are keeping track of this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In fact, that is our concern because there is some misinformation also spreading among young people, even amongst adults, thinking that e-vaporisers are harmless; that, in fact, they could be cessation products.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The truth is that there is a lot of data that suggests that they are gateway products to smoking as well as to drug use.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, these are things that we need to continue building knowledge on and also disseminating information on.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can the Ministry elaborate on any plans to involve youth representatives or youth-led organisations in the development and implementation of anti-vaping campaigns on social media, ensuring that the message is relevant as well as relatable to the target audience?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Indeed, it is important for us to have an understanding and keep aware of the trends that are happening in the space.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Which is why when we did the vape-free campaign in 2023, we did work with National Youth Council (NYC) and the youth organisations to understand and appreciate the nuances that would be helpful.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We worked with social media influencers and the different platforms to make sure that the information that is given out there is curated and will be reaching the groups that we target.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Indeed, this is going to be a work in progress.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have already ongoing relations with the youth organisations and we have plans to continue building on these efforts.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And I hope that we will also continue to get support from Members in disseminating the information to the right target audience.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: My concern is really with regards to the monitoring of and regulating the influencers in promoting vaping products.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: From the accountability perspective, what measures are in place or what considerations would the Ministry take before holding such influencers accountable for promoting vaping products, especially if they are found circumventing advertising regulations?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: My second supplementary question is with regards to the legal and regulatory updates.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The onus is on these platforms to exercise due diligence and proactively remove vaping-related content that are targeted at Singapore residents.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We will continue to work with different agencies like MCI as well as IMDA.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, we are taking a multi-pronged approach on this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On the front, with the digital platforms, we are going upstream, we are trying to monitor, we are engaging with the platforms and we are also educating our people.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, I think this is something that we do need a whole-of-community support on, and we will do what we can to ensure that we will not let this take root in our community, but we do hope to get support from the community as well, to disseminate this message and to also extend the right information to the youths.
